I will still start from what has worked for me around Quzhou. After 38 years, I do not like making big changes all at once. On my 10.1 mu, I will keep most land in the wheat-maize cycle because that is the steadiest way for me to get grain and cash back, and I will leave a smaller piece for cotton because I have grown it before and I know how to manage it. With well irrigation, I do not want to be stingy on water for wheat and maize, because one missed watering can cost more than a little extra fertilizer. I also watch costs closely, so I will not chase very high input use, but I will not cut fertilizer too hard either. For seed, I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed, because these have done well locally, and for cotton I will use improved seed that people around me have already planted with decent results. On the wheat-maize land, I will keep fertilizer a bit stronger on nitrogen, because that is what pushes yield here, while still giving phosphorus and some potassium so the crop does not go weak. Cotton I will manage a bit more carefully on pesticide because insects can get bad fast, and if I wait too long I lose more money.
